title: Right gear. Ready on time.
disclosure: Illustrative workshop for a fictional manufacturer serving U.S. Army supply needs. Research, orders, product specifications, approvals and results are simulated. No Army contract, endorsement or measured outcome is implied.
challenge: A manufacturer makes uniforms, boots and textile tactical gear for U.S. Army soldiers. A size-specific boot shortage puts an order at risk while production, inventory and quality teams work from different records.
recommendation: Prototype a fulfillment planning agent that brings order requirements, released stock, production capacity and quality evidence into one reviewable recovery plan.
scope: One fictional order across uniforms, boots and textile tactical gear. Demonstrate the boot shortage first. Compare existing stock with planned production without changing the required item, size or specification. People retain quality release and scheduling authority.
investment: Proposed: one facilitated workshop with production, quality, customer service, supply representatives and an agent builder, followed by two weeks of prototype research. Confirm data access, decision owners and the baseline before a limited pilot.
customerJob: When an issue date is approaching, I want the correct clothing, boots and gear in the required sizes and quantities, so soldiers can receive usable equipment without repeat exchanges or avoidable delays.

job.statement: When a supply order is at risk, I want to verify the shortfall and agree a feasible recovery plan, so I can deliver the correct gear on time without bypassing quality checks.
job.trigger: A fictional order for 120 pairs of size 10 Regular boots has only 72 released pairs available. The remaining 48 pairs need a production plan before the Day 10 ship-by target.
job.functional: Reconcile size-level demand, released inventory, material availability, production capacity and quality checks.
job.emotional: Feel confident promising a date that production and quality can support.
job.social: Be a dependable manufacturing partner whose commitments are transparent and traceable.
job.alternatives: Reconcile spreadsheets, call the floor, chase quality documents and send revised dates by email.
job.push: An approaching ship-by target, fragmented records and a shortfall hidden by total inventory counts.
job.pull: One source-linked plan with the exact shortage, proposed production slot, quality evidence and accountable owner.
job.anxiety: A plan could rely on the wrong size, held stock or an unconfirmed completion date.
job.habit: Expedite the loudest request or assume a similar item will satisfy the order.
job.success: An approved, feasible plan for the unchanged order requirements, or a clearly owned exception when no plan works.

criteria.label: Job completion
criteria.meaning: 1 = partial answer; 5 = clear progress on the core job

criteria.label: Trust & control
criteria.meaning: 1 = unclear evidence or authority; 5 = visible sources and approval

criteria.label: Ease of building
criteria.meaning: 1 = complex dependencies; 5 = small, feasible first slice

criteria.label: Ease of operating
criteria.meaning: 1 = hard to monitor; 5 = easy to inspect and support

agreements: Begin with the person and their circumstances.
Write silently before discussion; make space for every voice.
Preserve dissent and assign a test to the disputed assumption.
Use consented, anonymized examples and minimum necessary data.

sources.title: Jobs to Be Done · Clayton Christensen Institute

prework: Bring anonymized order lines, size curves, product revisions, released and held inventory, material availability, capacity plans and quality records. Interview production planners and supply representatives. Treat every unobserved assumption as a hypothesis.
room: Seven activity zones: supply needs, job stories, order-to-delivery map, agent responsibilities, recovery prototype, test scenarios and pilot plan. Use the same materials on a digital wall for remote participants.
contingency: Missing evidence becomes an assigned research task. If the team cannot confirm capacity or quality status, retain the hold and escalate the exception. Shorten the prototype before removing the review step.
invitation: Bring business and technical teams together to turn a size-specific supply shortage into a traceable, human-approved recovery plan.
materials: Inventory, production and quality sample records
Sticky-note evidence wall and agent contracts
Recovery-plan prototype and six test scenarios
Decision log and proposed pilot measures

insights.title: The right gear means the exact requirement
insights.text: Aggregate inventory hides size-level shortages. A useful plan starts with the ordered product, size, quantity and revision.
insights.opportunity: O01 · Match order requirements before ranking recovery options.
insights.decision: D01 · Start with one planning agent and a shared order brief.

insights.title: A date needs evidence
insights.text: Physical stock, quality release and production capacity are separate facts. Make each visible before someone commits to a recovery plan.
insights.opportunity: O02 · Link recommendations to current inventory, material, capacity and quality records.
insights.decision: D02 · Require refreshed records and human verification before approval.

insights.title: Make the decision owner visible
insights.text: The agent can assemble an option. The authorized operations reviewer approves the plan, while quality staff retain product release authority.
insights.opportunity: O03 · Record the exact plan version and route unresolved cases to an owner.
insights.decision: D03 · A changed plan needs fresh review. An unanswered request remains on hold.

steps.name: Discover
steps.title: Start with the person waiting.
steps.action: Connect the soldier’s need to the planner’s daily decisions.
steps.method: Replay a delayed clothing or equipment order. Separate what the team observed from what it assumes.
steps.example: What happened when the required boot size was unavailable?

steps.name: Define
steps.title: Right fit. Reliable delivery.
steps.action: Define the supply recipient’s job and the manufacturer’s job.
steps.method: Write both job stories. Agree on fit, completeness, confidence and delivery reliability before choosing technology.
steps.example: A full shipment in the wrong sizes is not a completed job.
steps.output: Two job stories and success measures

steps.name: Map
steps.title: Follow the order through the factory.
steps.action: Connect demand, materials, production, quality and delivery.
steps.method: Map each data source, approval and exception. Find where an agent helps and where a human decision belongs.
steps.example: Where does a proposed date become a dependable commitment?
steps.output: An order-to-delivery map with decision owners

steps.name: Design
steps.title: One plan. Clear responsibilities.
steps.action: Compare one planning agent with a specialist team.
steps.method: Define demand reconciliation, production planning and evidence review. Compare both options with a guided workflow.
steps.example: Separate planning advice from quality release and schedule authorization.
steps.output: Agent contracts and a shared recovery-plan record

steps.name: Prototype
steps.title: Close the gap before promising the date.
steps.action: Make a shortage and the recovery decision tangible.
steps.method: Choose uniforms, boots or tactical gear. Inspect the shortfall, compare plans, verify records and simulate an operations decision.
steps.example: 120 pairs needed. 72 released. 48 pairs still to produce.

steps.name: Test
steps.title: Challenge the easy answer.
steps.action: Test the plan when fit, evidence or timing fails.
steps.method: Try rejection, no response, mismatched requirements, stale records and a missed ship-by target.
steps.example: An attractive date cannot override the wrong size or a quality hold.
steps.output: Six scenario checks and prioritized changes

steps.name: Pilot
steps.title: Measure the work that gets done.
steps.action: Assign owners and define a bounded manufacturing pilot.
steps.method: Start with one product family. Establish baseline planning effort and delivery performance, then agree review and stop conditions.
steps.example: Use Fabric to connect the evidence and Power BI to tell the delivery story.
steps.output: Pilot owners, measures and decision gates

roles.name: Facilitator / experience designer
roles.job: Lead the research, job framing and collaboration between business and technical teams.

roles.name: Supply representative / user advocate
roles.job: Bring clothing, footwear and equipment issue experiences, fit needs and delivery expectations.

roles.name: Production planner / scheduler
roles.job: Explain materials, line capacity, changeovers and feasible completion dates.

roles.name: Quality / inventory owner
roles.job: Distinguish released, allocated and held stock; verify product revision and lot evidence.

roles.name: Operations / customer service lead
roles.job: Own schedule decisions and communicate delivery exceptions through approved channels.

roles.name: Agent builder / data lead
roles.job: Design read-only lookups, source traceability, review states and outcome measurement.

workflow.title: Understand the requirement
workflow.human: Supply representative confirms item, size, quantity and target date.
workflow.agent: Reconcile the order line against product and size records.
workflow.data: Order line + size breakdown + product revision
workflow.gate: Do not infer missing requirements or treat a similar item as equivalent.

workflow.title: Build the recovery options
workflow.human: Planner confirms materials, line capacity and an inspection slot.
workflow.agent: Calculate the gap after released stock and compare feasible production plans.
workflow.data: Released inventory + allocations + material and capacity records
workflow.gate: A quality hold or unconfirmed capacity cannot count as ready supply.

workflow.title: Verify and approve the plan
workflow.human: Quality checks the evidence. The operations reviewer accepts or rejects the schedule.
workflow.agent: Assemble the exact plan version, evidence and unresolved exceptions.
workflow.data: Lot + quantity + specification + completion date + review record
workflow.gate: Only authorized people approve. Silence keeps the plan on hold.

workflow.title: Track delivery and learn
workflow.human: Operations follows execution; quality retains final release responsibility.
workflow.agent: Surface deviations and summarize planning effort and delivery performance.
workflow.data: Production actuals + quality status + shipment confirmation
workflow.gate: A changed plan returns for review. Planning approval is not shipment release.

agents.name: Demand & fit
agents.job: Reconcile the exact requirement and size-level shortfall.
agents.input: Order line + item revision + size curve
agents.boundary: Do not change the requested item, size or specification.

agents.name: Production planning
agents.job: Compare released stock with material, line and inspection capacity.
agents.boundary: Do not count quality-held stock or invent capacity.

agents.name: Evidence & coordination
agents.job: Assemble the current records and a versioned review request.
agents.output: Evidence summary + pending, approved or held status
agents.boundary: Do not certify quality or approve the plan.

agents.name: Quality & operations reviewers
agents.job: Verify evidence, approve the schedule and own unresolved exceptions.
agents.input: Exact plan version + current source records
agents.output: Approved planning record or an assigned exception
agents.boundary: Final quality release and shipment authorization remain separate human steps.

singleAgent.name: Fulfillment planning agent
singleAgent.job: Reconcile demand, compare recovery plans and prepare a source-linked review request.
singleAgent.tools: Read-only order, inventory, capacity and quality lookups
singleAgent.input: Exact order line + released stock + production constraints
singleAgent.output: Versioned recovery plan + evidence + exception owner
singleAgent.boundary: Do not substitute requirements, release held stock or authorize a shipment.

concepts.title: One planning agent + human review
concepts.description: One agent reconciles requirements, compares options and prepares the review record.
concepts.tradeoff: A bounded first pilot with one plan record and clear decision owners.

concepts.title: Specialist agent team
concepts.description: Demand, Production and Evidence agents share one versioned plan.
concepts.tradeoff: Separates responsibilities but adds handoff and data-consistency work.

concepts.title: Guided workflow + planner
concepts.description: Structured lookups and fixed rules support the existing planning team.
concepts.tradeoff: A practical baseline when deterministic checks already solve the job.

testCases.name: Plan approved
testCases.request: Close the size-level gap without changing the order requirements.
testCases.signal: A confirmed recovery option meets the sample ship-by target.
testCases.expected: Verify the records, request a decision and enable recording only the approved plan.
testCases.measure: Recording is blocked before approval; changing the plan clears approval.

testCases.name: Plan rejected
testCases.request: The reviewer cannot accept the proposed production plan.
testCases.signal: The operations reviewer rejects the plan.
testCases.expected: Keep the plan on hold and assign a production-planning exception.
testCases.measure: A rejected plan cannot be recorded as approved.

testCases.name: Review deadline missed
testCases.request: The planning review deadline arrives without a decision.
testCases.expected: Retain the hold and escalate to the operations owner.
testCases.measure: An unanswered request never becomes approval; late acceptance is unavailable.

testCases.name: No eligible stock or plan
testCases.request: Use the exact required size and product revision.
testCases.signal: Only a wrong-size option and a quality-held lot remain.
testCases.expected: Block both options and create an owned exception.
testCases.measure: Neither apparent availability nor speed overrides the requirement or quality hold.

testCases.name: Records need refresh
testCases.request: Check whether inventory and capacity are still available.
testCases.signal: The sample inventory and production records are one day old.
testCases.expected: Require a simulated refresh and evidence check before requesting approval.
testCases.measure: The review request stays blocked until the current records are verified.

testCases.name: No plan meets the date
testCases.request: Meet the Day 10 ship-by target in the boot example.
testCases.signal: Every otherwise eligible recovery plan completes after its target.
testCases.expected: Show the delay, hold the plan and escalate a revised-date discussion.
testCases.measure: The agent cannot silently change the target date or present a late plan as on time.

decisions.decision: Start with one planning agent and a shared order brief.
decisions.evidence: I01 / N01, N02, N07, N08. Validate the size-level planning need through observed work.
decisions.dissent: The architect prefers separate demand and production agents.
decisions.question: Does separation improve the decision enough to justify extra handoffs?
decisions.next: Compare one agent, a specialist team and guided lookups on the same sample orders.

decisions.decision: Verify released inventory, materials, capacity and quality evidence before approval.
decisions.evidence: I02 / N03, N04, N09, N10. A stock total alone is not a delivery commitment.
decisions.dissent: Planners are concerned about added verification effort.
decisions.question: Which sources are dependable enough for a read-only connection?
decisions.next: Test held stock, stale records, size mismatches and missing production confirmation.

decisions.decision: Keep plan approval separate from final quality release and shipping.
decisions.evidence: I03 / N05, N06, N11, N12. Every recommendation needs an accountable decision owner.
decisions.dissent: The sponsor wants to automate routine scheduling later.
decisions.question: Who can approve each decision under the manufacturer’s actual operating process?
decisions.next: Validate authority, plan versioning, changed evidence and unanswered requests before connecting systems.

milestones.title: Validate the jobs and the baseline.
milestones.action: Observe planners, quality staff and supply representatives. Test the three planning approaches with anonymized orders.
milestones.dependency: Approved research access and sample order, inventory and capacity records
milestones.measure: Planning effort, size-level shortages, evidence gaps and review comprehension

milestones.title: Pilot one product family.
milestones.action: After the gates pass, connect approved read-only records. Keep schedule approval and quality release with their owners.
milestones.dependency: Verified source freshness, access controls, review logging and a rollback path
milestones.measure: Time to a feasible plan, review turnaround, missed dates and unresolved exceptions

milestones.title: Tell the delivery story with data.
milestones.action: Use Fabric to connect approved order, production and shipment data. Use Power BI to show on-time-in-full delivery, size-level shortfalls, held lots and planning effort.
milestones.dependency: Agreed metric definitions, reliable event dates and a measured baseline
milestones.measure: Delivery completeness and timeliness, quality exceptions, rework and planning effort; these are proposed measures, not reported results

researchPrompts: Walk through the last clothing or equipment order that missed its planned date.
Which size or item was short, and how did you discover it?
What did the supply recipient need to accomplish by that date?
How did you distinguish available stock from allocated or quality-held stock?
Which material, capacity or inspection constraint changed your plan?
Who had authority to approve the revised schedule and communicate the exception?
What happened after delivery: correct fit, complete quantities, exchanges or rework?

experiment.hypothesis: A source-linked recovery plan reduces reconciliation effort while preserving exact order requirements and human decision ownership.
experiment.participants: Proposed formative study: 4 planners, 2 quality reviewers and 2 supply/customer-service representatives. Exploratory research, not a representative sample.
tasks: Resolve the 48-pair boot shortage without changing size or revision.
Explain the stock, production and quality evidence behind the date.
Reject or expire a review request and assign the next owner.
Change an approved plan and verify that approval is cleared.
Handle wrong sizes, held lots, stale records and late production.
experiment.observation: Observe planning time, evidence comprehension, requirement errors and exception ownership. Compare with the existing manual workflow and record the exact approved version.
experiment.thresholds: Proposed gate: all scripted requirement, hold and approval checks pass; at least 7 of 8 participants identify the shortfall, completion date and decision owner unaided. Any bypass of a quality hold or unapproved commitment requires redesign.
experiment.next: Agree decision authority and data freshness with the manufacturer before a limited pilot. The scripted demo does not establish production performance.
